Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Argon

Alphabet introduced Gemini 4 Argon on Wednesday, marking its most advanced AI model release yet. The new model offers frontier performance across complex workflows like software engineering, enterprise knowledge and cybersecurity defense.

Argon is currently being used internally by Google for memory efficiency at its data centers, quantum computing optimization and more. The company said the full release requires a phased approach and Google is engaging with the U.S. government to gradually expand access.

“We’ll continue to gather feedback from early testers as we iterate on guardrails before making Argon available to developers, enterprises, and consumers as soon as possible,” the company said.

Alphabet said it’s currently working on strengthening critical frontier safeguards, with a focus on defending against misuse and prompt injection attacks, monitoring for misalignment and hardening systems.

Argon will initially cost $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. The new model is expected to roll out “soon” following testing by trusted individuals.

Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), and XRP (CRYPTO: XRP) remain rangebound, while speculative capital has rotated into institutional-infrastructure altcoins over the past days.

Why Quant Is Leading the Rotation

Santiment on Tuesday flagged on X that whale wallets are piling into Quant (CRYPTO: QNT) at a record pace, with 645 transactions worth at least $100,000 hitting the network in a single day, the most ever recorded.

The reason is simple: Quant builds technology that lets banks move money and assets across different blockchain systems without switching platforms.

On Sept. 24, The Clearing House, the bank-owned network that handles trillions of dollars in daily U.S. payments, picked Quant to help power its new system for moving bank deposits on-chain.

Analyst Greg Lunt laid out the broader case on X, pointing to real banks and institutions already using Quant’s technology:

  • Murex — software used by 65 of the world’s 100 largest banks now includes Quant’s tools
  • Oracle — the tech giant added Quant’s technology to its own enterprise software for handling digital assets
  • Central banks — the Bank for International Settlements, Bank of England, and European Central Bank have all tested Quant’s systems for moving money across borders

Lunt also pointed out that Quant has a hard cap of just 14.88 million tokens in existence. With that little supply available, big buying can push the price up fast, which is part of why QNT is moving so violently right now.

Where the Rest of the Rotation Is Flowing

Santiment also flagged that The Graph (CRYPTO: GRT), a project that helps apps pull data from blockchains, saw 24 transactions worth $100,000 or more in a single day, its busiest day all year.

Meanwhile, Chainlink (CRYPTO: LINK), which helps blockchains talk to real-world data and other networks, touched a fresh high even as some smaller holders sold into the rally. Santiment reads that as bigger buyers stepping in to absorb the coins retail traders are selling for profit.

Chainlink also rolled out an upgrade this week to the technology it uses to move assets between different blockchains, a network that has already handled more than $24 billion in transfers to date.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt separately named Stellar a long-shot pick for the next several years, sharing a long-term monthly chart to back the call.

Why This Rotation Could Be a Warning Sign for Bitcoin

Glassnode reported that altcoin spot trading volume has climbed to nearly four times Bitcoin’s, the highest ratio since September 2025. 

They also noted similar bursts of risk appetite have often lined up with local Bitcoin tops in the past, though the ratio alone can’t predict a reversal.

OpenAI said individuals allegedly associated with Moonshot AI, the Chinese developer behind Kimi, were part of a broader campaign to extract "protected reasoning" from its AI models, using thousands of requests designed to reproduce information the company keeps hidden.

"It is unclear whether all operators we observed during the relevant time period originated from a single actor," OpenAI said in a security report on Wednesday. "However, we attribute a core cluster of the activity to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi."

The campaign began July 1 and intensified on July 24 and 25, when OpenAI recorded 16,000 requests tied to the extraction pattern from more than 4,000 users. OpenAI later identified similar activity across a broader cluster of more than 15,000 users and said it had fully disrupted the activity by July 28.

"The operators did not break our encryption, compromise a database, or gain direct access to stored user conversations," OpenAI said.

The company described the activity as "adversarial distillation," a technique in which outputs from one AI system are harvested to help train or improve another model.

In one method, operators took encrypted reasoning from one conversation and then prompted a model in a separate chat to decode and transcribe the concealed material. Independent security researchers also reported related vulnerabilities through OpenAI’s responsible disclosure program, the company said.

The concern extends beyond the theft of proprietary technology. OpenAI said extracted reasoning could allow another developer to reproduce some of a model’s capabilities without maintaining the same safety protections.

"Adversarial distillation poses safety and national security risks," OpenAI said. "Extracted reasoning could be used to train another model without preserving the safeguards applied to the original model’s user-facing outputs."

The disclosure comes as leading AI developers increasingly focus on protecting the technology and training methods behind their models. Anthropic has also faced concerns around attempts to obtain or replicate the capabilities of its Claude models as competition among AI developers intensifies.

OpenAI responded by taking action against accounts, strengthening onboarding and infrastructure checks and expanding monitoring for connected networks. It also closed a replay-style pathway that could allow someone holding another user’s encrypted reasoning to recover its contents. The company added controls designed to detect and pause streamed output that could expose protected reasoning.

The ChatGPT maker coordinated with third-party service providers when it detected related activity moving through external platforms and shared its findings with industry peers through the Frontier Model Forum and relevant government information-sharing channels.

OpenAI expects model-extraction techniques to evolve as AI systems become more capable and is continuing to expand defenses across tools, classifiers, refusal behavior and cloud partners.

Bloom Energy Signs Patch Deal

Bloom Energy Corp (NYSE:BE) is one of the hottest stocks in 2026, with shares up 220% year-to-date. The electric power generation company is an AI data center adjacent play and has also attracted attention from Rep. Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) (More on that below).

The clean energy company signed a patch deal with the Philadelphia 76ers that will have the company’s name on every team jersey, including those worn by James during the 2026-2027 season.

(NASDAQ:IREN), another data center-related stock. The Los Angeles Lakers and New York Knicks have $20 million patch deals in place, according to the report.

While Bloom Energy is headquartered in California, the company also has a manufacturing hub in Newark, Delaware, near Philadelphia, where some of the near 1,200 employees of that facility live.

"This is our second home," Bloom Energy CEO KR Sridhar said in a video interview, as reported by Sportico.

Bloom Energy will make a seven-figure community investment as part of the sponsorship and also be the jersey sponsor for the Delaware Blue Coats, the NBA G League team of the 76ers.

With James on the 76ers, Bloom Energy could soon become a household name for anyone unfamiliar with the company. The 76ers will play in a league-high 34 nationally televised games during the 2026-2027 season.

James new 76ers jersey is the most sought-after for the current season, according to CNBC.

  • July 24: Bought 10,000 shares
  • July 28: Bought 100 call options with a $100 strike price, June 17, 2027 expiration date
  • July 28: Bought 5,000 shares

Bloom Energy stock trades at $278.58 today, up significantly from the time of the purchase by the Pelosis.

On Wednesday, President Donald Trump recounted an account of how an Israeli plumber helped prevent a Flydubai jet carrying 174 people from crashing after an altercation between the pilots sent the aircraft into a steep descent.

Trump Recounts Israeli Passenger’s Role

Trump said he spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about the incident and described an "Israeli plumber" intervening after hearing screams from the cockpit.

"He took the stick, lifted it up and leveled out the plane before it crashed," Trump said.

The president added that the passenger had never flown a plane, but Netanyahu told him he watches the Canadian documentary television program "Air Disasters" also known as “Mayday.”

"He said he watches that show, Air Disasters," Trump stated, prompting laughter. "You know the show? It’s the craziest show… he learned from watching that show sort of how to fly."

The Times of Israel identified the passenger as Yaniv Hayun.

Flydubai Flight Plunges 16,000 Feet

Flydubai Flight FZ1073 was traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv when a violent confrontation erupted in the cockpit.

Israeli officials said the co-pilot stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, in what they described as an apparent attempt to bring down the aircraft.

According to flight-tracking service Flightradar24, the Boeing (NYSE:BA) 737 Max 8 dropped from about 33,000 feet to 17,000 feet in roughly a minute before eventually making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

Flydubai described the incident as an "altercation in the cockpit" and said crew members diverted and landed the aircraft safely.

Netanyahu Praises Indian Pilot

Netanyahu separately praised Machchhar, calling him a "true hero" for fighting back, opening the cockpit door and allowing passengers and crew to overpower the attacker.

"My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery," Netanyahu said.

The co-pilot was reportedly arrested and questioned by Saudi authorities. Authorities have not established his identity or motive.

Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU) said Wednesday that humanoid robots could become a major driver of memory and storage demand in the years ahead, a shift analyst Shay Boloor believes would be the turning point for physical AI demand.

MU’s Humanoid Memory Forecast

On Micron’s fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call, CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said autonomous vehicles are the first big use case for physical AI, requiring more than 200 gigabytes of memory and multiple terabytes of storage.

That shift, he said, is expected to extend to humanoid robots and other autonomous systems.

“Physical AI can become a significant driver of memory and storage demand by the end of this decade,” Mehrotra said, adding that several physical AI customers are already sampling Micron’s next-generation products.

The chipmaker is increasing investment in its technology roadmap to ensure it is prepared to capitalize on this opportunity.

The company expects first-half capital expenditure of around $25 billion after reporting $10.8 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter.

Liquidia Corp. (NASDAQ:LQDA) shares are trending on Wednesday night.

Shares of the North Carolina-based biopharmaceutical company edged 0.13% higher to $30.30 in after-hours trading on Wednesday.

In the regular session, LQDA closed at $30.26, down 57.19%, according to Benzinga Pro data.

The stock experienced an elevated trading session on Wednesday. Trading volume rose to 22.95 million shares, nearly 19 times its average volume of 1.21 million shares.

Court Backs UTHR on Key Patent Claims

On Wednesday, a federal court in Delaware ruled that two claims of a patent asserted by United Therapeutics (NASDAQ:UTHR) are valid and infringed by Liquidia, the company said in a press release. The litigation concerns Yutrepia (treprostinil) inhalation powder, Liquidia’s lead product.

The claims cover treating pulmonary hypertension with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) using inhaled treprostinil, including dry powder formulations. The remaining asserted claims were found invalid.

United Therapeutics filed the suit under the Hatch-Waxman Act. Both sides must submit a proposed judgment, including proposed remedies, to the court within one week.

Remedy Risk Hangs Over Yutrepia

Liquidia said potential remedies could range from removing the PH-ILD indication from Yutrepia’s label to broader limits on the product’s availability. United Therapeutics has asked the court for an injunction restricting Yutrepia on the market.

The company said it cannot estimate its financial exposure given possible appeals and further proceedings.

Liquidia CEO Roger Jeffs said, “We respectfully disagree with the Court’s decision regarding claims 1 and 14 and are fully prepared to pursue all available appellate options.”

Liquidia also plans to submit a supplement to Yutrepia’s New Drug Application to the Food and Drug Administration to remove PH-ILD from the label.

Yutrepia was approved in 2025 for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and PH-ILD.

Trading Metrics, Technical Analysis

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) of LQDA stands at 20.23.

The mid-cap biotech stock has gained 33.07% over the past 12 months.

LQDA is currently positioned at 12.34% of its 52-week range.

Market research platform Bull Theory said on Wednesday that a Republican loss in the November midterms could be the “trigger” that bursts the AI bubble.

AI Becoming More Dependent on External Financing?

In an X post, Bull Theory argued that the AI industry’s growth is heavily reliant on capital spending, with major hyperscalers, including Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL), expected to invest nearly $800 billion in 2026, up 10x from 2019.

Bull Theory, citing JPMorgan research, said AI spending is projected to consume 93% of hyperscalers’ cash flow in 2026, up from 33% in 2023.

Additionally, Hyperscalers are projected to issue about $250 billion in bonds in 2026, up from roughly $121 billion a year earlier.

“So AI is becoming more dependent on debt and external financing at exactly the wrong time,” Bull Theory noted.

Financing to Become Tougher?

Bull Theory then drew attention to rising borrowing costs, with the Federal Reserve raising rates to 3.75%-4.00% and Treasury yields reaching record highs.

The firm said that President Donald Trump has been pushing the Fed toward lower rates, and losing Congress “could weaken” his broader ability to push a “pro-liquidity” agenda.

“For an AI industry increasingly dependent on outside financing, that’s another major risk,” Bull Theory said.

Congressional Pressure on Capex to Increase?

Bull Theory said Trump has made rapid AI infrastructure expansion a “major part” of his policy, but a Democratic-controlled Congress could impose stricter oversight of power consumption, water usage and environmental impacts, potentially slowing capital spending plans.

Notably, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) has criticized Trump’s support for AI data centers, arguing American families should not face higher electricity costs to fuel Big Tech’s artificial intelligence expansion.

“A Republican loss wouldn’t reverse all of that overnight,” Bull Theory argued. “But it could add congressional pressure to an AI CAPEX cycle that is already becoming much more expensive to finance.

What Do Crypto Punters Think?

Polymarket bettors see little risk of an AI crash, assigning a 9% chance of the bubble bursting this year and 17% by June 30, 2027.

Sam Rines, Macro Strategist at WisdomTree, told Benzinga that a slowdown in hyperscaler capital spending would likely hit semiconductors and infrastructure providers hardest, putting  NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ: NVDA) at greater risk.
